[USER] User is interested in popular street food dishes to try in Bangkok.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended street food dishes in Bangkok:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Pad Thai: Best found at Soi Rambuttri and Chinatown.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Tom Yum Goong: Available at street stalls all over Bangkok.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Som Tam: Popular favorite, try at Soi Rambuttri.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Khao Moo Daeng: Found at Yaowarat Road in Chinatown.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Moo Ping: Grilled pork skewers found at Sukhumvit Soi 38.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Mango Sticky Rice: Try at the Chatuchak Weekend Market.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Kuay Teow Ruea: Found on Phahurat Road.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Grilled Seafood: Head to Khlong Toei market for fresh seafood.

[USER] User asks for recommendations for dishes suitable for someone less adventurous with spicy food.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended dishes for less adventurous eaters:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Khao Moo Daeng: Sliced pork and crispy pork belly with rice and sweet sauce.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Moo Ping: Grilled pork skewers, typically not very spicy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Mango Sticky Rice: A sweet dessert that is not spicy.  
[USER] User plans to try Khao Moo Daeng and Moo Ping.  
[USER] User asks for tips for trying street food in Bangkok for the first time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for trying street food in Bangkok:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Look for crowded stalls with locals for fresh food.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Be open to trying new things as part of the local culture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Carry small bills and change for vendors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Choose clean stalls with high food turnover for hygiene.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Street food is cheaper than restaurants; try multiple dishes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Ask vendors for recommendations if unsure what to order.
